name: Robbins–Monro iteration

symbols.meaning: k-th estimate of the root of g(w) = 0

intuition: Treat g as a black box: when the observed value is positive, step left; when negative, step right; shrinking steps average out the noise.
assumptions: Zhao's convergence theorem (Theorem 6.1) adds conditions on ∇g, on the coefficients (the same two sums as the core text's (2.7)) and on the noise.
significance: With g̃(w, x) = w − x and a_k = 1/k it is exactly the incremental average (2.3) of the core text.
pitfalls: Zhao's sign convention steps against g̃ (minus sign), whereas the core text writes updates as + α[Target − Old]; the two agree once g̃ = Old − Target.

verification.note: Zhao Chapter 6 PDF page 4 (printed 104); numeric example checked by sup-zhao-06-q001.
